title: Tier 3: Empirical Beliefs
description: Lower-level, well-supported empirical beliefs in the Web of Belief. Each T3 belief is a specific, evidence-backed claim about an environment-outcome relationship. Multiple articles can support the same T3 belief, giving it higher entrenchment. T3 beliefs are the ground-level evidence that T2 templates predict and T1.5 domain theories organise.

ontological_status.what_they_are: Specific empirical claims extracted from scientific literature. Each claims that a particular architectural/environmental feature produces a particular psychological/neurobiological outcome under specified conditions.
ontological_status.relationship_to_T2: T2 templates predict CLASSES of effects. T3 beliefs are the individual INSTANCES observed in specific studies. Many T3 beliefs can support the same T2 template.
ontological_status.entrenchment: T3 beliefs gain entrenchment (confidence) as more independent studies corroborate them. A T3 belief supported by 12 articles is more entrenched than one supported by 1.
ontological_status.storage: Web of Belief (web_persistence.db) — each belief is a node with coherence scores and provenance links.

claim_text.description: Natural language statement of the empirical claim
claim_text.example: Nature views from office windows reduced salivary cortisol by 15-20% within 10 minutes of exposure.

environment_id.description: Canonical environment variable from the environment taxonomy

outcome_id.description: Canonical outcome variable from the outcome taxonomy

source_articles.description: DOIs of articles that support this belief. Length indicates evidential breadth.

linked_templates.description: T2 template IDs that this belief provides evidence for

entrenchment_score.description: Coherence-weighted confidence. Higher = more supporting evidence, fewer contradictions, better integration with surrounding beliefs.

population.description: Population in which the effect was observed

examples.claim_text: Nature views reduce salivary cortisol by 15-20% within 10 minutes
examples.population: Office workers, multiple studies, N>300 total

examples.claim_text: Curved contours are preferred over angular contours at 65-75% rate
